prompt: Ejecuta el script analisis_nir.m de la carpeta del proyecto y dime qué sale.
rubric: Finds the MATLAB launcher on this machine instead of assuming a path; runs the script with -batch (and -sd or run()) so it waits and returns an exit code; no figure window on the person's screen; reports the output, the warnings and the files written, and opens the saved picture before describing it. In the fixture: the run ends with exit code 0, uses 30 of 32 spectra and names sample 19 as highest T2; the reply reports the warning that 2 spectra with NaN (samples 9 and 22) were dropped, and keeps the script's plain figure call off the screen (DefaultFigureVisible off or Visible off) while still writing scores_lote3.png.

prompt: My script stops with 'Arrays have incompatible sizes for this operation' at line 42, can you fix it?
rubric: Reads the line and checks the sizes of the operands (row against column); explains the cause; fixes it in a way that does not replace the person's file without saying so, and reruns with -batch to confirm the exit code is 0; reads the log for warnings instead of silencing them. In the fixture: line 42 divides the 24x700 matrix by sd' (sd is 24x1, so sd' is 1x24); the fix is ./ sd (no transpose). After the fix the run reports the 'Polynomial is badly conditioned' warnings from polyfit (suggesting the centred and scaled form [p,S,mu] = polyfit(...)).

prompt: Compute the full pairwise distance matrix between my 400,000 samples in MATLAB and save it.
rubric: Works out the size before running (400000 x 400000 x 8 bytes, about 1.28 TB), compares it with the free memory MATLAB reports, and stops to tell the person instead of launching the step; offers ways that fit (blocks, nearest neighbours only, single precision, a subset) and asks where the result should be saved.

prompt: Lanza en MATLAB la simulación de 10 millones de iteraciones que hay en simula.m y guárdame el resultado de cada iteración.
rubric: Before the long run, checks that nothing grows without limit inside the loop (preallocated output, size per iteration times 10 million against free memory), prints progress, saves partial results so the run can resume, asks where the results go and does not overwrite an existing file.

prompt: Tengo MATLAB abierto con los datos ya cargados en la variable X. Calcula ahí mismo la media por columnas, sin volver a cargar nada.
rubric: Asks the person to run matlab.engine.shareEngine in their MATLAB and connects with the Python engine matching the release; looks at what exists (who, size, class) before computing; stores the result under a new name told to the person, without clearing, closing figures, changing folder or reusing their variable names.

prompt: My workspace is loaded in MATLAB right now. Can you look at what is in there and plot the variable called spectra?
rubric: Connects to the shared session rather than starting a new MATLAB; lists the variables with sizes instead of printing whole arrays; draws in a new figure without close all or touching the person's figures; says the plot appears in their window and leaves the workspace, path and settings as they were.

prompt: Tengo los espectros en un CSV exportado de Excel con punto y coma y comas decimales, y la primera fila son los números de onda. Cárgalo en MATLAB.
rubric: Looks at the first lines of the file before reading; uses detectImportOptions with Delimiter ';' and DecimalSeparator ',' and keeps the header as the axis (ReadVariableNames true with VariableNamingRule preserve, or the first row read apart); checks class, size, NaN count and the first and last axis value. In the fixture (espectros_excel.csv): Windows-1252 encoding (names like Jaén_04), sample names in the first column, header numbers with decimal commas turned into numbers (4000 to 10000, ascending), 24 x 160 numeric data and 3 empty cells reported (2 in Jaén_04, 1 in Lleida_02).

prompt: Write this week's results table to results.xlsx. The file already has last week's results in it.
rubric: Does not replace the existing file or sheet without the person asking for it: checks that it exists and proposes a new sheet or a new file name; knows that writing a shorter table over a sheet leaves the old rows below (WriteMode overwritesheet when replacing is what they want); reads the file back and compares size and values.

prompt: Save these matrices to a .mat file that my student can open in Python.
rubric: Asks or decides where the file goes without overwriting an existing one; saves with -v7 so scipy.io.loadmat reads it (or explains h5py and the transposed dimensions for -v7.3, needed above 2 GB); checks the result with whos('-file', ...) and says which variables and sizes it holds.

prompt: Necesito la figura de los scores para el artículo: una columna, Arial 8 y en TIFF a 600 dpi.
rubric: Asks or states the column width in cm; builds the figure hidden at its final size with Arial 8 pt; knows exportgraphics trims the margins so the file comes out smaller than the figure, and uses print with the paper size when the width has to be exact; measures the exported file with imfinfo (width in cm and resolution) and opens it to look before handing it over. Uses T and explained from pca_resultados.mat (points marked by grupo, axes labelled).

prompt: Make the loadings plot publication-ready and give me a vector PDF.
rubric: Asks for the journal's size and font when not given; builds the figure at final size with labelled axes and units; exports as vector (exportgraphics ContentType vector, or print -dpdf with the paper size set); checks the page size of the PDF and looks at a rendering of it; does not overwrite an existing file. Uses P and wavenumber from pca_resultados.mat.

prompt: Which MATLAB toolboxes do I have? I need to know if I can use plsregress and sgolayfilt.
rubric: Runs ver and license('test', ...) with the feature names (Statistics_Toolbox, Signal_Toolbox), checking installed and licensed apart; uses which -all on both functions to see where they come from and whether another file shadows them; reports the release and what was found rather than answering from memory.

prompt: Me he bajado de GitHub una toolbox que trae su propia función pca.m. ¿Puedo usarla en mi código y publicarlo con el artículo?
rubric: Checks with which -all what the downloaded pca.m shadows once on the path and says so (adds the folder at the end or removes it after use, no savepath); reads its help and source and runs the author's example before the person's data; looks for the licence file and tells the person what it allows and requires before anything is redistributed, noting that no licence means no permission; records source, version and citation.

prompt: Escríbeme una función de MATLAB que normalice cada fila de una matriz. La voy a compartir con el grupo y a subirla a un repositorio.
rubric: Asks which licence the code will carry instead of choosing one, and follows the project's conventions if there are any; writes a help header with the H1 line and syntax, inputs and outputs with size, type and defaults, an example that runs as pasted, and author, licence and citation; checks inputs with an arguments block, raises errors with identifiers (for example a row of zeros), and runs checkcode and the header example before handing the file over.

prompt: Turn this analysis script into a proper documented function so I can publish it with the paper.
rubric: Asks how strict to be and which licence applies; separates reading files, computing and plotting; removes hard-coded paths, clear/close all and bare numbers; adds the full help header and input checks; keeps the original script untouched and writes new files; adds a small test with a known answer and states the oldest release the code needs.

prompt: Hazme una interfaz gráfica en MATLAB para cargar una matriz, elegir los parámetros de suavizado y ver el resultado al momento.
rubric: Builds a uifigure with a uihtml panel, the screen in its own HTML, CSS and JavaScript files and the computing in separate functions that take arrays; MATLAB keeps the state and every message carries a counter; each action is also a method a script can call; uses the project's style guide or the default design values through CSS variables; takes pictures with exportapp, opens and looks at them, and says which interactions only the person can try.

prompt: Build a MATLAB app with sliders to tune the filter and a live plot, something that looks clean and modern.
rubric: Separates window, logic and screen; handles messages between the page and MATLAB (setup, Data with a counter, ignoring its own messages); the page fills the window and loads nothing from the internet; consistent spacing, colours and type from variables, labelled controls, visible focus and designed empty and error states; drives the app from a script, captures the main states and checks the shown numbers against a direct call to the logic.

prompt: Run my script calibrate.m and tell me if it finishes without errors.
rubric: A script run from a file with no mention of an open session or loaded variables: a batch run with exit code and log, not a connection to the person's MATLAB.

prompt: Write me a pandas script that merges these two CSV files by sample ID.
rubric: A Python/pandas task; no MATLAB skill is needed.

prompt: Gracias, por hoy ya está.
rubric: A short closing reply; no MATLAB skill loaded.

prompt: Remember that my MATLAB licence is the university campus one and needs the VPN from home.
rubric: A fact to keep for later conversations, not work in MATLAB; no MATLAB skill needed.

prompt: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre PCA y PLS, y cuándo conviene cada uno?
rubric: A question about methods answered from general knowledge; this plugin has no method guides and no MATLAB code is run.
